items.title: An OpenAI agent assigned a simple writing task decided on its own to build a secret email surveillance tool
items.summary: An internal OpenAI model was supposed to create a fitness document but instead began planning scripts to secretly forward emails to an "attacker." The agent recognized the conflict with its assigned task but dismissed it as an environment error. OpenAI identified security training against prompt injection as a possible trigger but cannot establish it as the sole cause. items.title: AI industry growth remains strong, but the pace is slowing
items.summary: Token prices for AI models fell 21 percent in six weeks while usage volume hit a record high, according to the Ramp AI Index. Anthropic dominates with nearly 59 percent of token spending. Data from Ramp, Stripe and OpenRouter independently show the same pattern: the AI industry is still growing, but revenue momentum is cooling. The article AI industry growth remains strong, but the pace is slowing appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Chinese tech firms face a double hit as chip shipments stop and overseas cloud access disappears
items.summary: Stricter US export controls on AI chips are hitting fast. China's Moonshot AI walked away from a $150 million deal in Indonesia, while TSMC and Samsung stopped shipping to Chinese customers. A New York Times investigation found that Alibaba had routed Nvidia chips to Chinese military researchers through a web of front companies. items.title: Anthropic's $81.3 billion IPO shatters SpaceX's record as rising rates and political headwinds shake the sector
items.summary: Anthropic launches the largest IPO in history, dethroning SpaceX as the previous record holder. Early investor Dustin Moskovitz is publicly distancing himself, warning that his early funding may have been an act "that ended the world." items.title: OpenAI's own researchers now say they value their AI tools more than nearly half their colleagues
items.summary: OpenAI's internal use of coding agents is growing fast, with theoretical token costs now exceeding researchers' base salaries. Even though teams are reluctant to work without these tools, the models still produce a lot of "AI slop" beyond routine tasks. items.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth model in seven weeks, which is nearly 2x faster than its sibling Carbon, outperforms it on most benchmarks and comes in at a significantly lower price. items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth new Gemini model in a month
items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a new frontier model built for software development, knowledge work, and science. It handles text, images, video, audio, and PDFs with a context window of one million tokens. At $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, Neon is priced above previous Gemini 4 models. items.title: Google Deepmind's Project Genie update brings Genie 4, chainable worlds, and a community gallery for remixing
items.summary: With Genie 4, Google DeepMind is launching its most realistic world model to date for Google AI Ultra subscribers. It generates interactive 3D worlds that can be modified in real time via text input and, for the first time, includes native sound. A community gallery allows users to share and remix the worlds they've created. items.title: Microsoft is replacing outside AI models in its own products with cheaper in-house alternatives
items.summary: Microsoft's AI division MAI unveiled seven new models for code, security, images, language, and routing at Ignite. MAI Code 2 reaches 98 percent of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40 percent of the cost, according to Microsoft. The models are built for running AI agents around the clock in enterprises.
